domain_setting: A calm nutrition-education space with a kitchen counter, simple tableware, fresh foods and non-judgmental health cues.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use a 304×192 scene with a clean plate, glass, small bowl or produce basket as scale anchors where relevant.
Keep food and nutrient scenes practical and recognizable; no packaging brands, readable words, letters or numerals.
Use only simple pictorial bars, icons and portions for nutrition comparisons; do not make unsupported nutrient or medical claims.
Keep weight-related language neutral and non-judgmental; use number-free scale cues and avoid changing body shape as a value judgement.
Use the chapter group to resolve ambiguity: salt and diet refer to nutrition, iron to a nutrient, fiber to dietary fiber, fat to food nutrients, and detox to a diet trend rather than a medical cure.

polysemy_resolution_table.calcium: Dietary mineral in food such as milk, yogurt or leafy greens; not a metal specimen.
polysemy_resolution_table.calories: Energy in food, shown with a simple food-and-energy comparison without numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.carbohydrates / carbs: Food group represented by bread, rice or potatoes; not a chemical diagram.
polysemy_resolution_table.cholesterol: A dietary and blood-health nutrient concept; use food context and a simple vessel or measured symbol without implying one food alone determines health.
polysemy_resolution_table.energy: Vigor supported by eating; not electricity or abstract spirit.
polysemy_resolution_table.fat: Fat as a nutrient in food; not body size or shame.
polysemy_resolution_table.fiber: Dietary fiber in plant foods and whole grains; not thread or textile fiber.
polysemy_resolution_table.iron: Iron as a mineral nutrient in foods such as beans or leafy greens; not metal bars or tools.
polysemy_resolution_table.minerals: Nutrients found in a variety of foods; not geological rocks.
polysemy_resolution_table.nutrition: The process of taking in nourishing food, in a balanced meal context.
polysemy_resolution_table.protein: Protein as a food nutrient, represented by beans, eggs, fish or other foods without a text label.
polysemy_resolution_table.salt: Edible table salt used in food; not the arms-control acronym.
polysemy_resolution_table.saturated fat: Food fat commonly solid at room temperature, shown in a small food portion such as butter or cheese.
polysemy_resolution_table.sugar: Edible sugar crystals or spoonfuls used in food; not a blood-sugar diagnosis.
polysemy_resolution_table.unsaturated fat: Food fats in plant oils, nuts or avocado, distinguished from solid saturated fat by their liquid or plant-food form.
polysemy_resolution_table.vitamins: Micronutrients represented by a varied set of fruits and vegetables, not medical pills alone.
polysemy_resolution_table.convenience food: Ready-made food prepared for quick use; not an appliance or shop.
polysemy_resolution_table.dairy: Milk-based foods such as milk, cheese and yogurt; not dairy farming.
polysemy_resolution_table.fruit: A recognizable assortment of edible fruits.
polysemy_resolution_table.legumes: Edible plants and their seeds, including beans and peas.
polysemy_resolution_table.processed food: Food changed or packaged for preparation and storage; show the food product rather than machinery.
polysemy_resolution_table.pulses: Dried edible legume seeds such as lentils, chickpeas and beans.
polysemy_resolution_table.superfoods: A nutrition-marketing category for nutrient-dense foods; avoid claims of special powers or cures.
polysemy_resolution_table.vegetables: Edible vegetables, not fruit used botanically.
polysemy_resolution_table.water: Drinking water as part of a healthy diet.
polysemy_resolution_table.whole grains: Grains retaining their bran and germ, represented by whole-grain bread or intact kernels.
polysemy_resolution_table.allergic to something: A mild visible reaction to a food trigger such as peanuts or shellfish; no severe distress.
polysemy_resolution_table.allergy / allergies: Food allergy in this nutrition lesson; show a trigger food and a mild reaction, not the prior cat-trigger scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.balanced diet: A meal with varied food groups in reasonable proportions.
polysemy_resolution_table.calorie-controlled diet: A meal plan with measured portions and energy awareness, without readable counts or extreme restriction.
polysemy_resolution_table.dairy-free: A meal choice without dairy, using a clear plant-based alternative; not a medical claim.
polysemy_resolution_table.detox: A cleanse or detox diet trend as a term; depict food and drink choices without claiming they remove toxins or cure illness.
polysemy_resolution_table.diet: A person’s eating plan or pattern; not a national parliament.
polysemy_resolution_table.gluten-free: A meal without wheat or gluten-containing grains, with a clear alternative such as rice; no readable labels.
polysemy_resolution_table.pescatarian: A diet including plant foods and fish while excluding meat from land animals.
polysemy_resolution_table.vegan: A diet excluding meat, fish, eggs and dairy; show plant foods as the meal.
polysemy_resolution_table.vegetarian: A diet excluding meat and fish while allowing plant foods and possibly eggs or dairy; distinguish from vegan.
polysemy_resolution_table.cut down on something: Reduce an amount of a food or drink, shown by a smaller serving or moving some away.
polysemy_resolution_table.eat something in moderation: Enjoy a small portion alongside a varied meal; distinguish from cutting an item down over time.
polysemy_resolution_table.give something up / give up something: Stop choosing a particular food or drink, shown by setting it aside and choosing an alternative.
polysemy_resolution_table.good source of something: A specific food paired with a nutrient cue, without text or unsupported claims.
polysemy_resolution_table.healthy: A person feeling well alongside varied food and water; not an idealized body type.
polysemy_resolution_table.healthy eating: A varied, balanced meal and a calm eating context.
polysemy_resolution_table.high in something: A food with a strong/high pictorial nutrient indicator compared with a reference; no numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.low in something: A food with a small/low pictorial nutrient indicator compared with a reference; no numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.portion: One measured serving on a plate, distinct from the whole dish or package.

Milk, cheese and another dairy product form a clear food-group scene.
Recognizable assortment of edible fruits in a bowl.
The existing produce assortment was recognizable, but an unrelated horizontal stroke crossed the vegetables. Rebuilt the produce scene and removed the stray line.
Glass of drinking water with a water drop; clear beverage and nutrition-context match.

reviewed_candidates.verdict: REJECT for 70:allergy / allergies; use as visual reference only

glossary_context_notes: The Japanese gloss for salt and diet reflects unrelated homonyms; the lesson group fixes the nutrition senses.
The legacy allergy illustration is not reused because the trigger must be food in this chapter.
Keep weight-related scenes neutral and number-free. Avoid suggesting that individual foods detoxify or cure.
Salt, sugar, dairy, fruit, vegetables and water are adapted from clear existing exact-term scenes; all other terms will receive context-specific art unless triage identifies a clearer match.

Full-size review refined calcium and carbohydrate scenes: calcium now has a clear long-bone silhouette beside milk and leafy greens; carbohydrates show bread, potato and rice. The first reviewed batch is complete.

Batch 2 had no exact-term SVG candidates. Fat uses food forms of oil and butter without body-size cues; fiber uses an apple and oats; iron uses leafy greens and beans rather than metal; minerals uses varied food sources; nutrition shows the eating process.

Batch 3 contains the two reworked exact-term candidates salt and sugar plus three new scenes. Protein is shown with beans, fish and egg. Saturated fat is a small solid butter-and-cheese serving, while unsaturated fat uses avocado, plant oil and nuts to distinguish the categories.

Batch 4 reuses the clear milk/cheese/yogurt dairy scene and fruit assortment, and adds produce-based vitamins, a ready-to-serve covered meal for convenience food, and a fresh leafy legume plant with visible peas. These were checked at full size.

Batch 5 reuses the cleaned vegetable assortment and clear drinking-water card. No exact-term candidates existed for processed food, pulses or superfoods: these are shown as tomato preserve in a package, dried seeds in bowls, and a varied platter without magical effects or claims.

Batch 6 had no exact-term candidates; the generic cat-trigger allergy from Lesson 69 remains rejected. Whole grains uses seeded bread and intact kernels. “Allergic to something” shows a mild reaction to shrimp; the allergy noun uses peanuts and a small skin response. Balanced diet is a proportioned varied plate; calorie-controlled diet shows several modest, measured meal portions.

Batch 7 had no exact-term candidates. Dairy-free uses an oat drink, detox shows a green juice trend without health claims, diet is a recurring meal pattern, gluten-free contrasts crossed wheat with a bowl of rice, and pescatarian shows fish with plants. Full-size review clarified the oat and rice cues.

Batch 8 had no exact-term candidates. Vegan uses only plant foods; vegetarian includes egg and cheese but no meat or fish. Cut down on something shows three cookies becoming one over a comparison arrow; moderation pairs a small cake treat with a varied meal; give something up shows setting aside a sweet drink and choosing water. The cut-down and moderation food silhouettes were clarified after review.

Batch 9 had no exact-term candidates. Good source shows a segmented orange paired with nutrient cues; healthy shows a well, comfortable person; healthy eating is a varied table meal with water; high/low are matched food-and-level cards with many versus few pictorial nutrient markers. Full-size review confirmed the matched level contrast and clarified the healthy-eating plate.
